name: Cassell Cruickshank
strengths: Cruickshank fires low off the ball — first-step burst that gets him skinny through the B-gap before the tackle sets inside hands.
Cruickshank uses 6-5 length to swipe and create separation, then flattens down the line on backside chase with long closing strides.
Cruickshank keeps pad level for his height on inside moves and shows JACK versatility — hand-in-dirt 5/9 and standup off the edge.
Cruickshank finishes with motor — multiple backside pursuits across the field and backfield penetration that meets the ball carrier at the mesh.
weaknesses: Cruickshank still needs SEC mass on a 6-5 / 217 frame — can get washed on doubles and down blocks until the anchor catches up.
Cruickshank’s rush plan is still mostly speed and length — needs tighter counters beyond the initial get-off.
comparison: Cruickshank comps to Boye Mafe — long 6-5 EDGE mold; first-step burst, length to create separation, and a frame built to fill into every-down rushes (size-matched within ~1–2" of Cruickshank’s 6-5 / 217).
projection: Cruickshank projects as Year 1 package / JACK rushes who develops into the EDGE rotation, then competes for starting snaps — ceiling as a long, explosive SEC every-down edge whose pass-rush package catches up to the traits.
schemeFit: Cruickshank fits wide-9 / JACK EDGE who wins with burst and length while the frame fills.
insiderNotes: Cruickshank is a long 6-5 EDGE with first-step burst, active length, and JACK versatility. Fires low, gets skinny through gaps, and runs to the ball on the backside. Florida leads his On3 RPM board with Bam Hardmon on the offer.
